reading.body:
CyrusOne Houston holds 84 MW of IT capacity across HOU3 and HOU4, the largest published data center campus in Texas among the 19 facilities that disclose power figures.

The campus spans 347,000 square feet of technical space and carries a Green Globes certification, which signals energy efficiency operations but says nothing about AI workload readiness. Its 84 MW equals 18 percent of the 475 MW of published IT capacity across those 19 Texas facilities, and it ranks first among them. At 40 kW per rack, that is roughly 2,100 racks; at 10 kW per GPU, about 8,400 high-end accelerators if fully allocated to GPU compute.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, but the vast majority publish no power figures, so the full state capacity is unknown. CyrusOne Houston's rank is first only among disclosed facilities, not necessarily among all. The campus's grid connection and whether it can sustain AI training loads are not published, and its suitability score of 77 reflects missing announced expansion data.
